Polylactic acid (PLA) is typically synthesized through a condensation polymerization process. The polymerization of lactic acid to form PLA involves the reaction between the carboxylic acid group (-COOH) of one lactic acid molecule and the hydroxyl group (-OH) of another lactic acid molecule. This reaction produces an ester linkage and releases a small molecule (water) as a byproduct.

The release of a small molecule (water) during the polymerization process is the defining characteristic of condensation polymerization. In contrast, addition polymerization involves the addition of monomer units to a growing polymer chain without the elimination of any byproducts.

Therefore, the polymerization reaction leading to the formation of polylactic acid (PLA) is characterized as a condensation polymerization.
